title: Approaching Carnot Efficiency at Finite Power in an Experimentally Feasible Quantum Heat Engine
authors: Shogo Toma, Atsushi Noguchi, Ken Funo, Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract: Whether a heat engine can approach Carnot efficiency while maintaining finite power is a fundamental question in finite-time thermodynamics. For classical Markovian heat engines with local interactions, the power-efficiency trade-off forbids an asymptotic approach to Carnot efficiency at finite power. In quantum systems, by contrast, degeneracy, symmetry, and collective jumps have been theoretically predicted to enable such an asymptotic attainment by enhancing activity. It has remained open, however, whether this mechanism can be realized in an experimentally implementable heat engine. In this Letter, we propose a superconducting-circuit heat engine that emulates the collective enhancement, thereby enabling an asymptotic approach to Carnot efficiency at finite power. This result demonstrates that, in an implementable model, such an enhanced dissipative mechanism circumvents the power-efficiency trade-off of classical Markovian engines. Our work connects abstract bounds in finite-time thermodynamics to a concrete circuit-QED platform and suggests a route toward quantum-device design based on collectively enhanced dissipative processes.
summary: This paper shows that by engineering collective enhancement mechanisms in a superconducting circuit heat engine, one can circumvent the classical power-efficiency trade-off. The authors demonstrate that the engine can approach Carnot efficiency while still producing finite power, confirming theoretical predictions using an implementable quantum platform.
main_problem: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether a quantum heat engine can approach Carnot efficiency while operating at finite power, overcoming limitations faced by classical Markovian engines.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that using a superconducting-circuit platform and exploiting collective enhancement mechanisms allows the engine to achieve $\eta = \eta_C - O(1/N)$ while maintaining $P = O(N)$.
method: The work combines theoretical derivation of thermodynamic quantities (heat, work) with numerical simulation on an effective quantum master equation describing the working medium.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting-circuit heat engine utilizing two coupled cavities and a qubit, emulating collective enhancement via a coupler-assisted swap (CAS-$c$) interaction. The dynamics are modeled using the GKSL equation under various approximations.
key_observables: Efficiency ($\eta$), Power ($P$), Heat current ($J$), Work rate ($\dot{W}$), and Entropy production ($\Sigma$).
important_parameters: The scaling parameter $N$ (total photon number) is crucial, as the result holds in the limit where $\eta - \eta_C = O(1/N)$ and $P = O(N)$.
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the Born–Markov approximation, adiabatic elimination of auxiliary cavities, and operating within specific dispersive parameter regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (cavities, qubit), the two-stroke cycle protocol in phase space, and numerical confirmation showing $P \propto N$ and $\eta_C - \eta \propto 1/N$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the classical power-efficiency trade-off to proposing a quantum mechanism (CAS-$c$), deriving an effective master equation for the working medium, and finally demonstrating analytically and numerically that this mechanism achieves the desired scaling limits.
why_interesting: This work directly connects abstract thermodynamic bounds in finite-time physics to a concrete, experimentally realizable platform (circuit-QED), providing a blueprint for designing quantum devices based on enhanced dissipative processes.
